abstract:
Abstract
                  As brands seek to increase racial representation in their advertising, many are turning to AI‐generated images of humans (i.e., synthetic models) as a scalable solution. This research demonstrates that consumer reactions to synthetic models are asymmetric, depending on the racial identity being depicted. Across five studies, we demonstrate that disclosing the AI‐generated nature of models lowers firm evaluations when the featured models are from racially underrepresented groups (e.g., Black, Hispanic, and Asian models), but not when they are White. This effect is driven by reduced perceptions of the authenticity of the firm's inclusion efforts, which in turn elevate inferences of manipulative intent. Importantly, these negative effects can be mitigated when consumers are informed that the firm is owned by members of the depicted racial community, suggesting that credible signals of authentic community ties can neutralize the evaluative penalty of AI disclosure. Our findings extend research on racialized depictions in advertising by identifying synthetic depiction as a novel threat to the evaluative benefits of minority representation, and by theorizing why this threat operates asymmetrically by race. More broadly, our results highlight that technological innovations in advertising cannot be divorced from the social and historical contexts that shape their meaning.

ob.ai_reason: AI生成广告模特的消费者反应，核心营销+AI
ob.tldr: 品牌在广告中使用AI生成合成模特以提升种族代表性，但五项研究显示，披露AI生成身份会显著降低消费者对企业评价，且该效应仅在模特属于种族少数群体（黑人、拉丁裔、亚裔）时出现，白人模特则不受影响。机制在于降低了消费者对企业包容努力的真实性感知，进而引发操控意图推断。若告知企业由该种族群体成员拥有，可消除该负面效应。

ur.ai_reason: 5项消费者研究，AI广告种族表征效应
ur.tldr: 五项研究揭示消费者对AI生成合成模特广告反应存在种族不对称性：披露AI生成身份会降低品牌评价，针对黑人、西班牙裔、亚裔等少数族裔模特时尤为显著，因其削弱包容真实性感知并引发操纵意图推断；若品牌由所描绘种族群体所有，则可中和该负面效应。

title:
